items.title: Single point of failure aur redundancy: ek cheez girne se sab kyun band hota hai
items.one_idea: A single point of failure is any one part with no backup whose failure stops the whole system; you find it by asking 'if this dies, does everything stop?' for each part on the request path, and you remove it by adding a redundant copy, but the catch is that the switch-over to the copy (failover), the detection of the failure and the extra cost can themselves become the next weak spot.

items.hook_formula: relatable_stake: the viewer's own app going dark because one thing broke, stated as a plain fact with no question after it
items.hook_10s: एक ही server गिरा, और पूरा app बंद हो गया। इसे कहते हैं single point of failure: एक ऐसी चीज़, जिसका कोई backup नहीं। चलिए देखते हैं, ये कैसे पकड़ें और कैसे हटाएं। [frame 0: a row of four boxes (phone, server, database, payment) with one red box going dark and the whole row turning grey]

items.visual_idea: One fixed frame: a chain of boxes (user, load balancer, one server, one database) where one box turns red and everything after it goes grey; then the same box gets a twin beside it, the red one dies and the arrows reroute to the twin so the chain stays green. A last step shows the switch box itself with a single arrow into it, turning red, and gets its own twin.
items.everyday_anchor: A whole building or mohalla losing power because it has one transformer and no second line, or a shop with one billing counter and one card machine: when it stops, nobody can pay.
items.example: EXAMPLE: one server that is up 99% of the time. Two such servers running side by side, where either can serve, are both down only 1% x 1% = 0.01% of the time, so about 99.99% (formula 1 - (1 - X)^N from Wikipedia High availability). It holds only if the two fail independently; two servers on one power socket or one rack do not. EXAMPLE numbers, not from a real company.
facts_to_verify: SPOF definition: a part whose failure stops the whole system and has no backup (Wikipedia Single point of failure)
Redundancy can be at component, system and site level (Wikipedia Single point of failure)
Redundancy = intentional duplication of critical components; active vs passive (Wikipedia Redundancy (engineering))
The crossover point itself tends to become a single point of failure (Wikipedia High availability, second principle)
Formula 1-(1-X)^N and its independence assumption (Wikipedia High availability; Redundancy (engineering) says the formula assumes independent failures); recompute 99% x 2 = 99.99% by hand
Common-cause failure example: two power supplies on one socket (Wikipedia Redundancy (engineering))
AWS: replace one large resource with multiple small ones so they do not share a common point of failure (Well-Architected reliability pillar, design principles)
Perrow quote that redundancy adds complexity is a contested view: say 'adds complexity', do not claim redundancy lowers reliability in general
The cost of redundancy is not stated in the fetched pages: say it as plain reasoning (twice the servers), not as a sourced figure
No real company outage or internal design is named; any company mention needs its own fetched post
